proposal:
VERDICT: I found no credible universal mechanism, and the general goal is still missing. I pivot from the fixed-degree two-field closure to one prime-free invariant with deliberately narrow scope. Nothing below was executed.

MECHANISM IALH-k (integer affine lattice hull).
Windows: every variable set S with |S|<=k that is a union of at most two clause supports. The complete variant uses all k-subsets.
Local table: T_S = assignments t in {0,1}^S for which unit propagation on F plus t gives no conflict. Every satisfying assignment restricted to S lies in T_S. An empty T_S means UNSAT.
Representation: integer unknowns x_1..x_n and lambda_{S,t} for t in T_S, with equations sum_t lambda_{S,t} = 1 and x_i = sum_t lambda_{S,t} t_i for i in S. All coefficients are 0/1. With B windows there are E <= B(k+1) equations and N <= n + B*2^k unknowns.
Operation: decide integer feasibility by Hermite normal form computed modulo a determinant bound.

Lemma A (soundness). A satisfying assignment gives a 0/1 solution, with lambda the indicator of its restriction. So infeasible implies UNSAT. The certificate is a rational u with u*A integral and u*c non-integral, checkable without trusting the solver.
Lemma B (all moduli at once). A congruence a.x = b mod m (m=0 meaning equality) holds on T_S iff it holds on the hull, because integer affine combinations preserve congruences. By Smith normal form the hull is cut out by exactly these congruences. So the system is feasible iff all window-entailed integer congruences, for every modulus together, are consistent. No prime list and no syntactic XOR pattern is needed.
Lemma C (limit). If T_S is the cube minus one point p (a lone clause of width >=2), the hull is all of Z^S, since p = a+b-c on a 2-face. Clause-only windows are provably useless; all power comes from multi-clause windows.

Hand checks:
1. Exactly-2-of-4 has hull {sum=2}, which gives the even parity the syntactic extractor missed.
2. Neon block: allowed signed weights are {0,3}. Weight-3 vectors generate every e_i-e_j plus a vector of sum 3, so the hull is {sum = 0 mod 3}. Each 5-variable block is the union of two of its 4-variable clause supports, so k=5 finds it. Taking u=1/3 on the seven congruences gives 3*sum(x1..x11)+1 = 0 mod 3, which is infeasible.
3. Weights {0,4} on five literals give sum = 0 mod 4, which GF(2) and GF(3) linear algebra cannot see.

Integration with SCC-E-MRA: run after Canon and SCC, at root and after every branch. Fixing x_i=v and finding infeasibility yields a unit (2n solves). If both unequal fixings of a pair are infeasible, the literals are equivalent; if both equal fixings are, they are complementary. These feed the existing complement-preserving contraction. Optional tuple pruning deletes t from T_S when x_S=t is infeasible, with at most B*2^k deletions. All derived facts are entailed, so the state key, equal-residual merging and survivor history are unchanged.

Bit length and work (an obligation, not proved here): Hadamard bounds every subdeterminant by (2^k+1)^(E/2), about E(k+1)/2 bits, and modular HNF keeps entries within that. A crude count is O(E^2 N) arithmetic steps on O(Ek)-bit integers, roughly B^5 k^6 2^k bit operations per solve. That is polynomial in encoded length for fixed k, since B <= m^2. The constants must be checked against Kannan-Bachem and Domich-Kannan-Trotter, which I cite from memory.

FALSIFIABLE HYPOTHESIS H.
(i) On the 175-clause Neon instance, SCC-E-MRA+IALH-5 refutes at root with zero branching (current receipt: peak 4).
(ii) Inconsistent block mod-m systems for m in {3,4,5} with k=6 are refuted at root by the same code.
(iii) Controls: non-onto pigeonhole 5-into-4 and threshold random 3-CNF show frontiers identical to the current solver.
H fails if (i) or (ii) needs a branch, or if splitting clauses to width 3 hides the blocks from the two-support window rule.
missing_theorem:
First unsupported claim U1: for some fixed k, SCC-E-MRA+IALH-k has polynomially many frontier nodes on every CNF. I have no argument for U1 and expect it to be false.

Lemma C already shows that formulas whose windows each carry one clause give a trivially feasible system, so the search there is exactly the old one. Most windows of sparse random 3-CNF at constant k are of this kind. At-least-one and at-most-one pigeonhole windows also have full hulls.

The promise-CSP literature on affine integer relaxations (AIP hierarchy, BLP+AIP, CLAP) includes limits by Berkholz-Grohe and Lichter-Pago. As I recall them, unchecked, such relaxations fail even on some tractable group-coset CSPs. Transfer to this CNF encoding is not justified here.

Absent and needed:
(M1) a potential function bounding distinct residuals after lattice closure;
(M2) a discovery theorem that polynomially many windows expose all affine structure under clause splitting;
(M3) any handling of non-affine hardness.

The general polynomial-time SAT algorithm is still missing.

Narrower target worth proving and checking in Lean: Lemmas A-C plus an explicit bit bound for modular HNF on this 0/1 system. Its scope is window-affine structure only. It matters because it would replace the parity and mod-3 extractors the solver lacks with one certified invariant.
self_attack:
1. This is not new mathematics. It is the affine integer programming relaxation known from promise CSPs; the novelty is only relative to this project.
2. It is a fixed-window relaxation, the same species as bounded width or fixed degree. It is one more structure detector, unified but still a detector, and I do not present it as universal.
3. 'All moduli' holds only inside the window. Detecting sum = 0 mod m needs more than m literals in one window, so the 2^k cost rises with the modulus.
4. Discovery is the weakest point. The two-support rule is heuristic and clause splitting can defeat it. The all-k-subsets variant makes B about n^k, so the work bound becomes roughly n^(5k), polynomial but impractical.
5. The HNF bit bound and operation count are from memory. Naive integer elimination explodes coefficients, so an implementation must use modular HNF and be checked independently.
6. Comparison with degree-3 closure over GF(2) and GF(3) is unproved. For moduli 2 and 3 that closure probably subsumes this. The claimed gain is other moduli and integer equalities at a state size linear in the number of windows.
7. The hull computations are hand-checked only. The mod-4 and mod-5 test families are not yet constructed, and small inconsistent instances may be awkward to build.
8. Per-node overhead of 2n plus O(n^2) feasibility solves could dominate the branching it saves.
9. The fixture is null. The mechanism differs from the current SCC-E-MRA target, the Neon instance exceeds 100 clauses, and my earlier hand-predicted peak was wrong.
10. The source-watcher handoff contained nothing relevant to this mechanism. I treated it as untrusted and did not use it.
mechanism_signature: IALH-k: integer affine lattice hull of UP-filtered windows, modular-HNF feasibility, unit/equivalence feedback into SCC-E-MRA
delta_from_prior:
The prior round (DFC-d) was a degree-d monomial closure over the two fixed fields GF(2) and GF(3), with about n^d columns per field. The new mechanism is a single integer lattice system with 0/1 coefficients and n + B*2^k unknowns. It captures every window-entailed congruence for all moduli and integer equalities together (Lemma B) and comes with a rational Farkas-type certificate.

It addresses the two specific prior failures. Semantic truth-table hulls replace syntactic XOR-block extraction, so the Exactly-2-of-4 parity is found. The Neon mod-3 instance is predicted to be refuted at root rather than at peak 4.

Also new: Lemma C, a provable statement of where the mechanism gives nothing, and experiment H with a composite-modulus family (mod 4) that no GF(2) or GF(3) linear extractor handles. There is no claim of universality.
